q: How does a real estate developer count emissions from flats it sells?
title: Developer: emissions from sold flats
short: Materials like cement, steel and glass are the developer's purchased goods, Category 1, counted when bought. Contractors' site diesel and power are Scope 3 unless the developer runs the site. Residents' electricity after sale is use of sold products, Category 11, usually estimated over the building's expected life.
audience: Real estate developers and their lenders

ul: Embodied carbon: materials by quantity from bills of quantities.
Use: expected annual electricity per flat × years × grid factor.

p: Category 11 rests on assumptions about use and grid change; state them.

senseible: Senseible keeps purchase invoices on the Scope 3 trail with the category, method and factor source on every line, so spend-based estimates are labelled as estimates and can be replaced with supplier data later.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard
